newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends at 83-month low on dlr build-ups.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends at 83-month low on dlr build-ups.

text.p: The won closed at an 83-month low against the dollar on Thursday, backed by strong dollar build-ups stemming from the belief the dollar was undervalued, dealers said. "Banks bougtht dollars despite the central bank's dollar sales," said a domestic bank dealer.
The won ended at 864.20, the lowest closing since the nation introduced the market average system in March 1990, after opening at 859.00. It touched a high of 858.60.
The Bank of Korea sold dollars twice -- at 859.20/50 late in the morning trade and at 865.50 late in afternoon trade to slow the won's decline, dealers said.
The bank denied intervening, as it routinely does.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 862.00 on Friday, compared with 859.60 today.
Dealers said the dollar demand continued to rise in line with the U.S. unit's strength against the Japanese yen on world markets and the nation's rising trade deficits.
"Long-term trend is set for the dollar's rise," said a foreign bank dealer. Expectations of tightening liquidity before the Lunar New Year Holidays next week would limit the won's fall, dealers said.
